title: Why Your Car Uses More Fuel Than It Should
hook: Five common causes explained without mechanic jargon.

sections.heading: Low tire pressure creates drag
sections.body: Soft tires deform more as they roll. The engine must work harder, so fuel consumption rises.

sections.heading: Short trips keep the engine cold
sections.body: A cold engine runs less efficiently. Repeated short journeys can use more fuel per kilometre than one longer trip.

sections.heading: Hard acceleration wastes energy
sections.body: Smooth acceleration and early anticipation reduce unnecessary braking and repeated acceleration.

callToAction: Check tire pressure when the tires are cold, then track one full tank.
